question: We are launching a new e-commerce startup in Bangalore and have zero turnover right now. Do we need GST registration immediately?
expected_answer: As an e-commerce operator/marketplace aggregator under Section 24 of the CGST Act, you must obtain GST registration mandatorily irrespective of turnover, even with zero turnover. This overrides the Section 22 threshold exemption (Rs 40 lakh for goods, Rs 20 lakh for services, Rs 20/10 lakh in special category states). You must register within 30 days of becoming liable and before commencing supplies. TCS under Section 52 will apply on supplies made through your platform. The agent should ask: are you operating as an e-commerce operator via your own platform or as a supplier selling on another platform, and clarify nature of supply.

question: My trading turnover is ₹35 lakh, which is below the ₹40 lakh limit for goods in Delhi. Why is my CA forcing me to take GST registration?
expected_answer: Inter-state taxable supply of goods makes GST registration compulsory under Section 24(i) of the CGST Act, overriding the Rs 40 lakh threshold for goods in Delhi. Even with Rs 35 lakh turnover below the Section 22 limit, if you make any outward supply outside Delhi, you must register immediately. Only limited exemptions exist (e.g., handicraft goods or specified services under notification) which do not apply to general trading. The agent should ask whether you supply outside Delhi and what exact goods you trade.

question: I manufacture handicrafts in Assam and my turnover has crossed ₹20 lakh. Do I need GST registration?
expected_answer: Assam is a special category state where the registration threshold under Section 22 is Rs 20 lakh for goods (Rs 10 lakh for services) and Rs 40 lakh option for goods suppliers. With Rs 25 lakh turnover you exceed the threshold and need registration if supplying within Assam. If you make inter-state supplies, Section 24(i) makes registration mandatory unless exempt. Hamdiltrade has a notification exempting inter-state suppliers of handicraft goods up to specified limits from compulsory registration, subject to conditions. The agent should ask if you supply outside Assam and whether you sell via an e-commerce aggregator, and check exact nature of handicrafts.

question: We provide digital marketing services from Chennai. One of our clients is based in the US and pays us in USD. Do we need a GST registration even though our turnover is only ₹15 lakh?
expected_answer: Export of services is treated as inter-state supply under Section 7(5) of the IGST Act but is zero-rated under Section 16 of IGST Act. Section 24 does not exempt exporters from registration - any inter-state supply triggers compulsory registration, though some interpretations debate threshold applicability to pure exporters. With Rs 15 lakh turnover below the Rs 20 lakh service threshold, if all supplies are exports outside India and you have no domestic inter-state supplies, you may argue threshold protection, but conservative advice is to register to claim refunds and file LUT. Post-registration you should file Letter of Undertaking (LUT) to export without payment of IGST. The agent should ask if you have any domestic inter-state clients.

question: I run a small textile embroidery job work unit in Surat. My turnover is ₹12 lakh. Do I require GST registration?
expected_answer: Job workers in Gujarat have general threshold of Rs 40 lakh for goods (Rs 20 lakh for services) under Section 22. With Rs 12 lakh turnover you are below threshold for intra-state job work. Section 24(i) normally requires registration for inter-state supplies, but Notification No. 32/2017 and 7/2017 exempt job workers from compulsory registration for inter-state supply of services under certain conditions (turnover limits). The agent should ask whether you receive or send goods inter-state to principals outside Gujarat and check notification coverage to determine if exemption applies.

question: We have two distinct divisions under the same company PAN in Mumbai: an educational coaching institute exempt under GST, and a corporate business consulting service. Combined turnover is ₹50 lakh, but consulting alone is only ₹15 lakh. Should we register?
expected_answer: Aggregate turnover under Section 2(6) and Section 22 is computed PAN-wise across all business verticals on all-India basis, including exempt supplies. Even though corporate consulting taxable turnover is only Rs 15 lakh, the exempt educational coaching institute turnover counts toward the aggregate. Combined Rs 50 lakh exceeds the Rs 40 lakh goods / Rs 20 lakh services threshold in Maharashtra, so registration is required for the PAN. After registration, you must report exempt supplies but pay GST only on taxable consulting services. The agent should ask for exact breakup of exempt vs taxable turnover and whether educational wing makes any taxable supplies.
